court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: I Additional Family Judge, Chennai - HMOP.No.1596 of 1997
facts_of_case: Marriage between the Petitioner-husband and Respondent-wife was solemnized on 04.12.1994. The Petitioner-husband filed a petition for dissolution of marriage under Sec.13(1) (i-a) of Hindu Marriage Act, alleging cruelty by the Respondent-wife.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the respondent to prove that she was treated cruelly.
legal_principles.held: Finding that Respondent-wife treated the Petitioner-husband cruelly, trial Court arrived at the conclusion of 'cruelty' mainly on the following grounds:-

legal_principles.principle: A respondent's conduct can be considered cruel if she leaves the matrimonial house without informing her husband.
legal_principles.held: Respondent has left the matrimonial house without informing him.

legal_principles.principle: Filing a private complaint with false allegations of demand of dowry can be considered cruel.
legal_principles.held: Respondent has filed private complaint making false allegation of demand of dowry which was taken on file in C.C.No.630/1998

outcome.final_order: The Family Court has allowed the Petition filed under Sec.13 (1) (i-a) of Hindu Marriage Act dissolving the marriage of the Appellant-wife and Respondent-husband on the ground of cruelty.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on grounds for divorce in Chennai courts
assisting with appeal against family court order
